questions.q: What is the main purpose of this article?
options: To argue that willpower matters more than environment design
To compare popular habit-tracking apps and notebooks in detail
To share short reader stories showing how people apply habit-building ideas
To review the Habit Journal product and its templates
questions.explain: The author shares 30 short stories from Atomic Habits readers showing real people building habits.

questions.q: How did one reader practice Mandarin while living in China?
options: He practiced with online lessons every day during his spare time
He struck up conversations with taxi drivers on each ride
He joined a weekly language-exchange group and spoke with partners every weekend
He reviewed flashcards during his daily commute to and from work
questions.explain: He committed to strike up a conversation with the taxi driver whenever he took a cab, doing it for two years.

questions.q: How did Daniel make himself get out of bed without hesitation?
options: He asked a friend to call him every morning at six
He placed his phone in the garage until morning came
He slept in his running clothes and went straight out
Scanning a QR code in the bathroom turned off his alarm
questions.explain: The only way to turn off his alarm was scanning a QR code in the bathroom.

questions.q: How did Qiana quit drinking soda?
options: She told herself she would quit only until her next cheat day
She replaced soda with juice, tea, then seltzer over months
She locked the soda in a car parked out in the cold
She scooped the week's soda sugar into a big bowl to see it
questions.explain: She added up the sugar in a week of sodas and scooped it into an enormous bowl.

questions.q: What does the author imply about habit substitution with exercise?
options: Replacing a habit works better than gradually cutting back
Exercise is never unhealthy, however much a person does
Substitution is useless against serious drug or alcohol addictions
Swapping in exercise can be a healthier obsession than drinking
questions.explain: He suggests substitution can give you a healthier obsession, noting exercise is generally better than hours spent drinking.
